decisions.resolution: Explicit user decision 2026-10-04: keep shipped Mobile lineage. Audit and compatibility patch descend from ede1f2a0ccf75f3794c7892f291e1751b279d19e; do not integrate unrelated newer Mobile payment flows.

decisions.conflict: Legacy signup treated supplied matching or absent artist email as verified ownership; session helper committed outer credential mutations before issuing tokens.
decisions.resolution: Reject anonymous artist adoption; route independent accounts to reviewed management. Serialize credential transitions and remove the read-only token-reuse/early-commit behavior. This is a security repair, not specification approval of existing bugs.

decisions.conflict: Backend directory administration accepted module-only actors; claims allowed self-review, separate transaction status checks and approval replay that restored revoked grants.
decisions.resolution: Enforce the declared Admin role plus module and reviewer separation. Preserve multi-role Admin composition. Serialize review, grant, audit and response; identical-state retries are read-only. Do not redefine concurrent rejected/approved mismatches as valid product behavior. Implement the existing full claim transition graph, including evidence requests; keep every review edge Admin-only and same-state retries observational. Exhaust the declared graph through HTTP.

decisions.conflict: Ignored Hpack input declared version 1.0.0, a library and executable tdf-hq; actual Stack and image builds use hand-maintained Cabal version 0.1.0.0, executable tdf-hq-exe and test suite.
decisions.resolution: Archive the stale Hpack description outside the active package. Stack snapshot remains toolchain authority. No switch to a Cabal CLI build and no regeneration from the retired input.

decisions.conflict: Image recipes disabled Debian package authentication and metadata freshness to tolerate network failures, allowing untrusted build/runtime inputs.
decisions.resolution: Remove the bypasses and require fail-closed APT verification in both image recipes. Diagnose proxy/mirror trust failures instead of weakening package trust.

decisions.conflict: Fixed-width products and sums can wrap to a positive value accepted as a parent total despite the declared exact line-total invariant. Per-line PostgreSQL checks do not enforce the cross-line aggregate.
decisions.resolution: Repair application calculations with exact arithmetic and explicit narrowing checks; retain cross-line database enforcement as an open additive-migration obligation. Do not redefine wrapped amounts as valid.

decisions.conflict: Generic parent-subtotal equality would reject shipped merchandise shipping represented as both header fee and payable line. Fixed-width arithmetic can disagree with exact monetary equations.
decisions.resolution: Require exact payable-total equality at the database boundary; preserve existing shipping representation and floor commission while repairing unchecked intermediates. Historical applied SQL remains unchanged; use additive migrations.

decisions.conflict: Consolidated main fdac8e765 adds provider payment behavior and a Mobile gitlink that competes with the explicit shipped-lineage decision. Prior audit evidence describes the pre-consolidation tree.
decisions.resolution: Integrate current root main and retain all six added payment migrations with historical introduction SHAs; append the three audit migrations. Keep Mobile descended from ede1f2a and regenerate compatible API and feature metadata only. Preserve prior receipts as historical evidence and rerun candidate checks; do not infer native payment parity or enable providers.

decisions.conflict: Historical cutover instructions still describe keeping production on Fly, while live identity and database are on Hetzner and the routine release command still executes Fly.
decisions.resolution: Archive the original cutover plan as historical evidence. Reject Fly preflight/release execution before remote operations; preserve source-only planning and shared validators. Add a repository-owned read-only Hetzner collector with fixed target, secret-safe output and negative controls. A complete guarded Hetzner release executor remains an explicit open obligation.

decisions.conflict: The chat adapter reports rejection after its database transaction has already committed. A real malformed-result regression retained a message and changed thread timestamp despite an HTTP error.
decisions.resolution: Keep session, SQL effects and response validation in one transaction; roll back rejected envelopes. Preserve existing non-idempotent transport-loss semantics and never-governed legacy compatibility. Add runtime negative controls and a bounded sequential model; do not redefine committed error outcomes as intended behavior.

decisions.conflict: Broad Scheduling module access allowed private foreign bookings despite own-booking persona intent; legacy edits bypassed the authoritative exclusion calendar and checkout snapshot.
decisions.authority: Product owner explicitly selected four studio-wide roles on 2026-10-04; formal/system/bookings.md
decisions.resolution: Require backend object scope; preserve four-role staff operations and own/assigned access, row-lock edits, repair allocation projection additively and reject checkout evidence drift. Document three previously missing authenticated API operations and regenerate both shipped clients.

decisions.conflict: The initial shipped-Mobile decision and its documentation referred to ede1f2a, but concurrent consolidated-main PR479 shipped Mobile147ec8bc with additional functionality.
decisions.authority: Product owner explicitly selected Use newly shipped Mobile pin after being shown root5efd7ff and Mobile147ec8bc.
decisions.resolution: Preserve root5efd7ff and Mobile147ec8bc ancestry; apply reviewed compatibility fixes at ff107462. Supersede the earlier lineage restriction only for this newly shipped pin, retain original-baseline evidence, and do not infer authorization to follow unrelated later Mobile-main changes or activate providers.

decisions.conflict: The historical checkout table declares failed terminal and draft initial; runtime explicitly supports no-charge retry and begins accepted checkouts awaiting_payment. The pure checkout helper differs and has no production caller.
decisions.authority: formal/system/payment-retry.md; user payment reliability requirements corroborated by existing runtime guards and PostgreSQL retry tests
decisions.resolution: Retire the old checkout table to historical_state_machines, label the pure helper as non-runtime reference, and formalize scoped retry admission with negative controls. Do not redefine every existing SQL transition as approved or claim the full checkout state machine is reconciled.

decisions.conflict: Compiled CombinedAPI declares GET /version twice with incompatible DTOs. The later unreachable Meta.BuildInfo omits commit identity and computes builtAt from request time.
decisions.authority: Current public OpenAPI Version schema, first served VersionAPI and canonical production identity verification
decisions.resolution: Remove only the shadowed Meta version route/type and stale mounting example; preserve the existing first-served VersionInfo handler and its source/build metadata validation. The generated compiled snapshot must confirm one version declaration; other competing routes remain open.

decisions.conflict: A second public radio-presence declaration contradicts the published inherited bearer requirement and cannot be reached behind the protected route.
decisions.authority: Published bearer security and verified current HTTP denial, preserving the existing privacy boundary.
decisions.resolution: Remove the unreachable public declaration/handler. Keep authenticated cross-party presence behavior. Do not broaden access by reordering branches. Add anonymous, invalid-token and authenticated HTTP controls.

decisions.conflict: The public subjects GET shadows the private includeInactive GET; even an administrator receives only active subjects.
decisions.authority: Distinct public active visibility and explicitly guarded ensureSchoolAccess management behavior.
decisions.resolution: Keep the current public route and make managed listing reachable at /trials/v1/subjects/catalog using the same existing school guard. Document both operations and regenerate both clients. Do not move private auth ahead of the public route or expose inactive subjects anonymously.

decisions.conflict: Artist worker and schedule target retired Fly; old runbook directs Fly release/rollback. The worker marks a batch with a sub-threshold failed item completed.
decisions.authority: Verified canonical backend identity and explicit user requirement that failed workers cannot report success.
decisions.resolution: Use canonical API default/schedule, retire obsolete operational commands in favor of current Hetzner procedure, and separate early-stop threshold from failed-run completion. Preserve schedule and publication opt-in, add actual worker regression and scoped bounded model. No production dispatch or feature activation is performed.

decisions.conflict: OpenAPI publishes25 merchandise-reputation operations whose Haskell types and handlers exist but are not in CombinedAPI; interpreting every documented route as currently shipped contradicts the explicit local-only rollout scope.
decisions.authority: Existing explicit synthetic-local-only domain scope, corroborated by compiled routing and current production nine flags observed disabled. Observation alone does not authorize intent.
decisions.resolution: Enumerate the25 deferred operations in canonical availability policy, require their continued absence and flag any other missing documented route. Preserve raw discrepancy counts; no feature or route is activated. Future mounting needs a reviewed scope decision and relevant domain gates.

decisions.conflict: Eleven empty responses were incorrectly documented204; nine DDEX operations still documented501 despite four implementedhandlers and five deliberately disabled503 paths. Shipped Mobile duplicated removed DTO fields. Canonical SQL issue guards conflict with core-era legacy NOT NULL; completion still wrote legacy result.
decisions.resolution: Preserve established200 empty-body acknowledgements and accepted client behavior. Fix actual validation SQL/transaction defects, canonical result reads and shipped Mobile adapters. Do not fabricate successful import/export availability or official profile validation.

decisions.conflict: A reorder returns409 for an invalid later item but earlier per-item transactions already committed; revision and audit remain unchanged.
decisions.resolution: Repair transaction atomicity and locked revision admission. Apply the existing OpenAPI incomplete-set rejection as the working authority; product-owner clarification was initially pending because the old implementation accepted subsets. Require every current item exactly once. Product owner explicitly confirmed the complete catalog item list on 2026-10-05; that policy ambiguity is resolved.

decisions.conflict: Authenticated Facebook/Instagram private payloads are copied verbatim into stderr operational logs.
decisions.resolution: Remove raw payload receipts; retain only fixed channel and event count after persistence. Preserve governed message records and mark historical log retention/remediation as unresolved, not silently repaired.

decisions.resolution: Absent or blank secret makes all four POST aliases unavailable503. Configured signature checks remain401 on invalid proof. Explicit synthetic keys replace implicit development bypass; no production key values or changes.

decisions.conflict: Existing Drive key/folder lookup silently returns a prior file for different bytes, name, MIME or actor and then attempts public sharing.
decisions.resolution: Treat conflicting success as a request-integrity bug. Bind newly created entries to actor and request; preserve legacy objects but reject their implicit adoption. Retain worker key format and explicit provider-concurrency exclusions.

decisions.conflict: Long-lived actor-independent query cache survives logout; actual component reproduction displays prior Party private response under next Party.
decisions.resolution: Replace and remount cache per security-scope occurrence. Preserve current query defaults but retire old client state. Bind auth expiration to request epoch; do not convert cached disclosure into intentional offline behavior.

decisions.conflict: Token changes clear a shared client, but old favorite/visit callbacks repopulate it and expose personal metadata to the next account.
decisions.resolution: Use per-occurrence clients and remount query consumers; keep the exact shipped lineage and existing retry semantics. Clearing a shared cache is insufficient isolation. No offline or provider exactly-once guarantee is inferred.

decisions.conflict: Fallback endpoints and shared playback/publish keys imply usable broadcasting without a provider authorization contract; Mobile error fallback fabricates local acceptance.
decisions.resolution: Contain native creation with unconditional503, withhold legacy event endpoints, quarantine UUID-path radio projections, retain cleanup and external listening, propagate remote mutation failures. Historical example is explicitly unverified. Provider re-enablement and prior-key revocation remain separate work. Product owner explicitly approved keeping broadcasting unavailable during repair on 2026-10-05.

decisions.conflict: Published email/30-day commitments lack current operational workflow/completion evidence; historical mobile docs and release sign-off are not fulfillment evidence.
decisions.resolution: Owner explicitly requested discovery or creation. Establish machine-readable operator lifecycle, guarded private ledger and runbook; retain original deadlines, record retention honestly, require effect and delivered-notice evidence before closure. Do not infer inbox monitoring, legal adequacy or executed deletion from a passing synthetic test.

decisions.conflict: Actual concurrent HTTP accepted eight same-version writes and emitted eight audit rows for one update; approval conflict lookup was unbound and terminal decisions could reopen.
decisions.resolution: Retain intended version/current-scope/dual-approval requirements and repair transactional handlers. Historical abbreviated lifecycle and broad invariants are incomplete obligations, not proof. Request IDs remain diagnostic; approval keys require full semantic binding.

decisions.conflict: Teacher list hides a synthetic payment and detail returns404, while metrics returns its12345 minor-unit amount and unassigned count.
decisions.resolution: Treat totals/counts as protected projections, reuse list scope/role filter, and restrict integration-failure aggregate to the selected branch and its manager actors. Preserve supported assigned-specialist workflow; no feature activation.

decisions.conflict: Synthetic Teacher manual creation returned201 with hidden other-branch payment amount and changed its operational title/status; arbitrary client correlation and metadata entered the trusted projector.
decisions.resolution: Separate client receipt keys from server projection keys, bind actor/scope/payload, reject control metadata and unassigned specialist creation, target one event, verify successful projection before commit. Preserve explicitly trusted same-thread WhatsApp identity progression and historical SQL.

decisions.conflict: ReadOnly list and detail disagree; incidental producer fallback and role precedence differ across reads; failure list leaks other branches and notes/retries use stale admission.
decisions.resolution: Use one explicit read-domain policy with action-specific union, preserve documented ReadOnly read but not write authority, default unknown producer domain grants to deny, and revalidate auxiliary command scope/current roles in the atomic transaction.

decisions.conflict: The shipped lease contract requires current unexpired authority, but transaction-stable time accepts completion after expiry during a lock wait. New fixture entrypoints also admit remote databases with the expected name.
decisions.resolution: Preserve historical SQL and append a lock-before-real-clock completion correction, verified by actual PostgreSQL negative control; require pre-connection destination and override guards on every direct fixture entrypoint.

decisions.conflict: The request fallback renders arbitrary exceptions, catches cancellation and can call the response callback twice; authentication activity also renders arbitrary persistence errors into admin diagnostics. Warp fallback invents wildcard CORS outside configured policy.
decisions.resolution: Use a cancellation-preserving fixed-diagnostic boundary, track response start, propagate after callback admission, and leave error-origin grants to request-aware CORS. Radio raw exception strings are discarded today, not a proven public disclosure, but cancellation and fixed internal failure values follow the same boundary.

decisions.conflict: Consolidated main182fe6a introduces reviewed analytics credential containment and retires transactional Offer metadata, while the audit register predates those changes.
decisions.authority: Approved main PR487 and explicit privacy/truthful-state audit requirements
decisions.resolution: Preserve main by normal merge and map PRIV-ANALYTICS-001/EVT-PRESENTATION-001 to current source/tests. Historical analytics and metadata observations are not combined-head or provider conformance evidence.

decisions.conflict: Current receipt code relabels currency without conversion and uses count-based concurrent numbering; receipt replay intent is unbound and missing from canonical OpenAPI.
decisions.authority: User monetary/concurrency invariants and immutable invoice financial evidence
decisions.resolution: Fix transactional implementation and additive constraints; preserve invoice money, bind explicit replay parameters and current authority; document actual mounted API. Do not redefine reproduced bugs as product intent.

decisions.conflict: Health documentation promised a database check while runtime unconditionally returned ok; OpenAPI described an absent version and omitted actual db field.
decisions.authority: Existing readiness intent and user deployment verification requirements
decisions.resolution: Repair the handler to query its application pool, bound cooperative waiting, preserve cancellation and return fixed503 failures. Correct the actual response contract and both generated clients; do not treat healthy as full release admission.

decisions.conflict: The historical compose canary shares the production database; the database-only rehearsal did not establish application startup or unavailable-database behavior.
decisions.authority: User isolated verification and current canonical operations safety requirements
decisions.resolution: Retain the shared-database compose service as historical/unadmitted for release testing; add an explicit optional application on the nonce-owned disconnected restore target. Keep default database-only receipts and full coordinated recovery exclusions explicit.

decisions.conflict: Main5c2e0bb28 now ships Mobile6297e3f1, seven additional mapped requirements and a consolidated migration order while follow-up233188726 adds receipt/readiness/recovery boundaries. Historical enrichment schema rollback instructions also compete with the current no-data-loss deployment authority.
decisions.authority: Approved main PR478, prior user instruction to retain newly shipped Mobile and the current canonical operations safety contract
decisions.resolution: Normal merge preserves every unique requirement and combines observation mappings/privacy. Main analytics scalar-label contract and event supersession remain authoritative. Mobile76d19fc merges the shipped pin with exact generated readiness/receipt compatibility; no unrelated Mobile branch is substituted. Preserve main migration order and historical entries/SQL, append receipt snapshot migration, and rerun actual rehearsal. Keep current enrichment deployment authority and omit duplicated destructive schema rollback instructions; no guarded executor or current-head success is inferred from historical evidence.

decisions.conflict: The 2026-08-13 revenue model declared quote states partially_refunded/refunded after deposit_paid and omitted accepted -> expired. The effective schema (all 184 manifest migrations applied) rejects both refund states, the domo_validate_quote_runtime_update trigger permits accepted -> expired, and no code writes a quote refund state.
decisions.authority: Accepted ADR-0114 (2026-08-18), which is Domo-specific and later: quote, payment and venue states are independent, and refunds are separate domain operations outside the first slice.
decisions.resolution: Correct the model to the trigger's transition relation. Deposit refunds belong to the canonical `refund` machine. The state-machine gate now checks the quote states and transitions against the migrated database.

decisions.conflict: The declared distribution and royalty_statement machines disagree with the distribution_release_version.state and royalty_statement.state CHECK sets (for example delivering/live_confirmation_pending versus package_generated/delivery_queued/sent; variance_review/rejected absent from royalty statements). No backend code reads or writes either table.
decisions.authority: No approved product decision selects either vocabulary; neither surface has runtime behavior.
decisions.resolution: Classify both as SPECIFICATION AMBIGUITY and NOT IMPLEMENTED. Record the exact differences as reviewed deviations so any further drift fails; reconcile before any distribution runtime is built. No schema change is made for an unused feature.

decisions.conflict: PRIV-RAG-001 named an anonymous assistant visitor and the booking conformance script asserted anonymous /ads/assist availability, while the only caller is the staff Social Inbox and anonymous responses included staff-authored ad conversation examples and unmetered paid-model calls.
decisions.resolution: /ads/assist requires authentication and hasSocialInboxAccess. PRIV-RAG-001 retains its retrieval boundary with authenticated staff as the assistant actor. A future public assistant requires its own reviewed endpoint.

decisions.conflict: The startup schema verifier required checkout.paypal.refunds and the Datafast webhook/refund gates to be disabled, while production enabled checkout.paypal.refunds for the PATCH CULTURE refund rollout. The running API kept serving until its first restart on 2026-10-07, when every start (old and new image) failed verification and production returned 502.
decisions.authority: Explicit product-owner decision on 2026-10-06: refunds and Datafast must remain enabled.
decisions.resolution: The verifier still requires all six provider gates to exist but accepts either state for PayPal webhooks/refunds and Datafast webhooks/refunds; only PlaceToPay and Payphone remain staged. The migration test asserts approved states are accepted and staged providers rejected. ADR-0128's 'keep disabled' guidance is superseded for production by this decision; its execution fences and evidence requirements are unchanged. The verifier never enables a gate: Datafast gates remain disabled in production until separately turned on.

decisions.conflict: Academy enroll/progress and referral claim were anonymous and identified the actor only by a submitted email, so anyone could create or alter another person's enrollment, progress or referral attribution, and the progress 404 disclosed enrollment.
decisions.authority: Explicit product-owner decision on 2026-10-06: require login.
decisions.resolution: The three write routes move to the authenticated API on unchanged paths and bind to party.primary_email of the signed-in account; a mismatching email returns 403 and an account without email returns 409. Public microcourse content and next-cohort reads stay public. No client called the write routes.

decisions.conflict: Public WhatsApp consent accepted any number without proof of control, recorded consent and messaged the number immediately, and exposed consent state and timestamps through a public lookup.
decisions.authority: Explicit product-owner decision on 2026-10-06: double opt-in.
decisions.resolution: Add confirmation_requested_at to whats_app_consent (additive); public requests become pending and activate only on a timely affirmative reply from the number; the public lookup is retired (410); public opt-out is a non-disclosing withdrawal. Existing consent rows are unchanged. Closes DEBT-PRIV-WHATSAPP-001.

decisions.conflict: PRIV-WHATSAPP-001 promised at most one confirmation request per number per 24 hours and that a person can confirm by messaging SI themselves. The implementation cleared confirmation_requested_at on every opt-out and confirmation, so the unauthenticated opt-out reopened the interval and allowed unlimited requests to any number; it also cleared the pending request when the provider rejected the send, so the success page's SI button could never activate consent; simultaneous first requests for one number could fail on the unique row.
decisions.authority: The 2026-10-06 double opt-in decision (AUTHORITY-052) and the requirement statement govern; the implementation behavior was a defect, not policy.
decisions.resolution: Withdrawal and confirmation keep the request instant; a request is invalidated by revoked_at at or after it. A rejected send marks only its own request pending_unsent, which stays confirmable for 1 hour and does not block a new request while unwithdrawn. Row creation is conflict-safe. No schema change. The 1-hour window is an engineering default pending product-owner confirmation.
